::: {#fig-parse-trees}

```{r}
#| label: parse-trees-alt
#| include: false
fig_alt <- paste(
  "Two parse trees, drawn with the root at the top.",
  "In the left tree the root plus has children times and the leaf c.",
  "That times has children plus and the leaf x.",
  "The plus below it has children times and the leaf b,",
  "and that times has the leaves a and x.",
  "In the right tree the root plus has children plus and the leaf c.",
  "That plus has two children, both times.",
  "The first times has the leaf a and a power node with leaves x and 2.",
  "The second times has the leaves b and x."
)
```

```{r}
#| label: parse-trees-plot
#| fig-alt: !expr fig_alt
#| fig-height: 4
# Each tree is a nested list: the first element is the node's label,
# and the remaining elements are its children.
times <- intToUtf8(215)
trees <- list(
  "(a * x + b) * x + c" = list(
    "+",
    list(times, list("+", list(times, "a", "x"), "b"), "x"),
    "c"
  ),
  "a * x^2 + b * x + c" = list(
    "+",
    list(
      "+",
      list(times, "a", list("^", "x", "2")),
      list(times, "b", "x")
    ),
    "c"
  )
)

# Leaves sit at consecutive x positions;
# each operation sits above the mean of its children.
layout_tree <- function(node, depth = 0, next_x = 0) {
  if (!is.list(node)) {
    return(list(
      nodes = data.frame(label = node, x = next_x, y = -depth, is_leaf = TRUE),
      edges = NULL,
      next_x = next_x + 1
    ))
  }
  nodes <- NULL
  edges <- NULL
  child_x <- numeric()
  for (child in node[-1]) {
    sub <- layout_tree(child, depth + 1, next_x)
    next_x <- sub$next_x
    child_x <- c(child_x, sub$nodes$x[1])
    edges <- rbind(
      edges,
      sub$edges,
      data.frame(
        x = NA_real_,
        y = -depth,
        xend = sub$nodes$x[1],
        yend = sub$nodes$y[1]
      )
    )
    nodes <- rbind(nodes, sub$nodes)
  }
  me <- data.frame(
    label = node[[1]],
    x = mean(child_x),
    y = -depth,
    is_leaf = FALSE
  )
  edges$x[is.na(edges$x)] <- me$x
  list(nodes = rbind(me, nodes), edges = edges, next_x = next_x)
}

laid_out <- lapply(trees, layout_tree)
tree_nodes <- do.call(rbind, Map(
  function(res, name) cbind(res$nodes, tree = name),
  laid_out,
  names(trees)
))
tree_edges <- do.call(rbind, Map(
  function(res, name) cbind(res$edges, tree = name),
  laid_out,
  names(trees)
))
tree_nodes$kind <- ifelse(tree_nodes$is_leaf, "leaf", "operation")
tree_nodes$tree <- factor(tree_nodes$tree, levels = names(trees))
tree_edges$tree <- factor(tree_edges$tree, levels = names(trees))

ggplot2::ggplot() +
  ggplot2::geom_segment(
    data = tree_edges,
    ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend),
    colour = "grey50"
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_label(
    data = tree_nodes,
    ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = y, label = label, fill = kind),
    size = 5,
    linewidth = 0
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(operation = "#CCE5F6", leaf = "#F9DDBF")
  ) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(
    ~tree,
    scales = "free_x",
    labeller = ggplot2::label_parsed
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(fill = "node type") +
  ggplot2::theme_void() +
  ggplot2::theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 12)
  )
```

The [parse trees](#def-parse-tree) of $(a x + b)\,x + c$ and $a x^2 + b x + c$.
Each operation is a node with one child per [argument](functions.qmd#def-argument), and the leaves are the symbols that are not operations.
The caret is the [power](algebra-basics.qmd#def-power) operation, which takes a [base](algebra-basics.qmd#def-power-base) and an [exponent](algebra-basics.qmd#def-power-exponent).

:::
